name: Humboldt Redwoods State Park
tagline: Drive the Avenue of the Giants with your dog. Hike without them.
summary: Humboldt Redwoods follows the standard California State Parks rule: dogs are welcome in campgrounds, picnic areas, parking lots and on park roads, but not on any trail. The good news is that the park's main attraction, the 32-mile Avenue of the Giants, is a road, so you can stop at pullouts and walk the shoulder under the biggest trees in the world. The Eel River day-use areas give you shade, picnic tables and river access too. What you cannot do is walk Founders Grove, Rockefeller Loop or any other grove trail with your dog.
verdict: Bring your dog for a scenic drive, a river day and a campground under the redwoods. If you want to walk the famous groves, plan on taking turns or leaving the dog at a kennel.

Burlington, Hidden Springs and Albee Creek; not the environmental camps

allowed.name: Avenue of the Giants (State Route 254)
allowed.detail: The 32-mile scenic road through the park is open to dogs on leash. Park at any pullout and walk the paved shoulder among the trees. Watch for traffic; it is a real road.

allowed.name: Campgrounds
allowed.detail: Burlington (year-round, next to the visitor center), Hidden Springs (summer, near Myers Flat) and Albee Creek (May to early September, on Mattole Road). Dogs must stay in your tent or vehicle at night.

allowed.name: Day-use and picnic areas
allowed.detail: Williams Grove, the California Federation of Women's Clubs Grove, Dyerville Flats and the other developed day-use areas with picnic tables and restrooms.

allowed.name: Eel River gravel bars next to day-use areas
allowed.detail: Williams Grove and the Women's Clubs Grove have river access from the picnic area. Keep the leash on and stay near the developed area; the park's rule is developed areas only.

allowed.name: Parking lots and pullouts
allowed.detail: Including the Founders Grove and Rockefeller Loop parking areas. You can see big trees from the lot, but the trail itself starts a few steps away and is off limits.

allowed.name: Mattole Road and other park roads
allowed.detail: The paved road west through Bull Creek Flats toward Honeydew is open to leashed dogs on the shoulder.

notAllowed.name: Every trail in the park
notAllowed.detail: Founders Grove, Rockefeller Loop, Bull Creek Flats, Drury-Chaney, Grieg-French-Bell, River Trail and all the rest. Carrying a small dog does not make a trail legal.

notAllowed.name: Environmental campsites
notAllowed.detail: No pets at the Hamilton Barn or Baxter environmental camps.

notAllowed.name: Visitor center
notAllowed.detail: Dogs wait outside. There is shade and a lawn next to the building.

notAllowed.name: Undeveloped forest
notAllowed.detail: Dogs cannot leave the road, parking lot or picnic area to explore among the trees.

notAllowed.name: Unattended anywhere
notAllowed.detail: Not at a campsite, not tied to a picnic table and not in a parked car.

hikes.name: Avenue of the Giants roadside stroll
hikes.why: The only way to walk among the giants with your dog. The stretch near the Founders Grove turnoff and the stretch through Weott have wide shoulders and little traffic early in the morning.
hikes.maps: Founders Grove Parking, Avenue of the Giants

hikes.name: Williams Grove to the Eel River
hikes.why: A short walk from the picnic tables to a wide gravel bar on the South Fork Eel. Shade, water and a swimming hole in summer. $8 day-use fee.
hikes.maps: Williams Grove Day Use Area, Humboldt Redwoods State Park

hikes.name: Nearby: Rohner Park, Fortuna
hikes.why: A city park 25 miles north with real trails through second-growth redwoods where leashed dogs are allowed. The closest proper redwood hike for dog owners. Check current rules when you arrive.

hikes.name: Nearby: Arcata Community Forest
hikes.why: Redwood forest owned by the city of Arcata, about an hour north, with a trail network open to leashed dogs. Worth the drive if your trip is about hiking.
hikes.maps: Arcata Community Forest Redwood Park trailhead

hangouts.name: Williams Grove
hangouts.why: The park's biggest day-use area: sunny and shaded picnic tables, grills, restrooms and a path to the river. 3 miles south of the visitor center.

hangouts.name: California Federation of Women's Clubs Grove
hangouts.why: Picnic grove with the Julia Morgan-designed Hearthstone fireplace and a swimming hole. Storm erosion has closed part of the lot; vehicles over 16 feet cannot enter.

hangouts.name: Dyerville Flats
hangouts.why: Where the South Fork meets the main Eel River. Restrooms, picnic tables, an overlook and lots of parking.

hangouts.name: Founders Grove parking area
hangouts.why: You cannot take the dog on the loop, but the lot sits right among old-growth giants, and the visitor center lawn is a few minutes away.

hangouts.name: Burlington Campground lawn and visitor center area
hangouts.why: Flat, shaded and next to the Avenue. A good place for an evening walk from your campsite.

rules: Keep your dog on a leash no longer than 6 feet, at all times.
Dogs stay in developed areas only: campgrounds, picnic areas, parking lots and roads. No trails.
Never leave a dog unattended, including at your campsite or in a parked car.
At night, dogs must be inside a tent or vehicle.
Pick up waste and put it in a trash can.
Keep dogs out of the visitor center and other buildings.
Store dog food in your vehicle or a bear-resistant locker, never in the tent.
Service dogs are allowed everywhere; emotional support animals follow the pet rules.

camping.name: Burlington Campground
camping.note: 57 sites next to the visitor center, open year-round. Reserve on ReserveCalifornia. The best base for dog owners.

camping.name: Hidden Springs Campground
camping.note: 154 sites near Myers Flat, open roughly Memorial Day to Labor Day. Pets OK in standard sites.

camping.name: Albee Creek Campground
camping.note: 40 sites on Mattole Road, 5 miles west of the Avenue, open early May to Labor Day. Quieter, with meadow views.

camping.name: Not allowed
camping.note: Hamilton Barn and Baxter environmental camps.

lodging.name: Best Western Plus Humboldt House Inn, Garberville
lodging.note: 20 miles south of the park. Pets allowed for a fee.

lodging.name: Motel Garberville
lodging.note: Simple pet-friendly motel, about 10 miles from Miranda.

lodging.name: Giant Redwoods RV and Cabin Destination, Myers Flat
lodging.note: Dog-friendly RV park and cabins inside the Avenue of the Giants.

lodging.name: Redcrest Resort, Redcrest
lodging.note: Pet-friendly cabins at the north end of the Avenue.

lodging.name: Redwood Riverwalk Hotel, Fortuna
lodging.note: Pet rooms with a fee and a fenced dog relief area. Handy for Rohner Park.

seasons.title: Late summer algae in the Eel River
seasons.detail: Toxic blue-green algae blooms have killed dogs in the Eel River in late summer and early fall. If the water is warm, slow and has green scum or mats, keep your dog out of it entirely.

seasons.title: Summer heat inland
seasons.detail: The river flats can hit the 90s in July and August. Under the redwoods it stays cool. Walk early and bring more water than you expect to need.

seasons.title: Spring and fall
seasons.detail: The best time. Fewer cars on the Avenue, cool shade, and the river is clean and running. Hidden Springs and Albee Creek may be closed, so book Burlington.

seasons.title: Winter rain and flooding
seasons.detail: The Eel River floods in big storms and parts of the Avenue and Mattole Road can close. Burlington stays open year-round, but check road conditions before you drive.

wildlife: Black bears live throughout the park. Keep dog food in the car or the campsite locker.
Mountain lions are present. Keep dogs leashed and close at dawn and dusk.
Ticks are common on grass and road edges; Lyme disease occurs in Humboldt County. Check your dog after every walk.
Poison oak grows along roadsides and river bars. The oil gets on fur and then on you.
Toxic algae in the Eel River in late summer (see Seasons).
checklist: A 6-foot leash, not a retractable one
Water for two and a collapsible bowl
Waste bags and a way to carry them to a bin
A towel for river mud and wet fur
A kennel booking in Fortuna or Eureka if you want to hike the groves
An ID tag with your mobile number; cell coverage is spotty along the Avenue
